Group-level whole-brain task fMRI contrasts from delayed response tasks measuring executive function (matching task). Contrast appears to compare task to a control (MAT>CONT), meeting pooled executive function criteria.
The matching delayed-response task measures working memory (visuospatial STM/WM) and the contrast compares task to a control condition (MAT>CONT), satisfying working memory inclusion criteria.
Task does not measure inhibitory control; missing required inclusion criteria INHIBITION_I1 and INHIBITION_I2.
Task is not a task-switching or set-shifting paradigm; missing required inclusion criteria COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I1 and COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I2.
Matching task involves maintenance rather than sequencing/organizing forthcoming actions; missing required inclusion criteria PLANNING_I1 and PLANNING_I2.
Task is not a sustained-attention/vigilance paradigm; missing required inclusion criteria VIGILANCE_I1 and VIGILANCE_I2.
Task does not target action/behavior initiation/generation (e.g., verbal fluency); missing required inclusion criteria INITIATION_I1 and INITIATION_I2.

Group-level whole-brain task fMRI contrasts from the reproduction delayed-response task, which requires executive control to prepare sequential actions; contrast appears to compare task to control (REP>CONT), meeting pooled executive function criteria.
Reproduction is a delayed-response working memory task (maintenance/manipulation) and the contrast compares task to control (REP>CONT), satisfying working memory inclusion criteria.
Task does not measure inhibitory control; missing required inclusion criteria INHIBITION_I1 and INHIBITION_I2.
Task is not a task-switching or set-shifting paradigm; missing required inclusion criteria COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I1 and COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I2.
Reproduction requires mental organization/sequencing of forthcoming actions during the delay, and the contrast appears to be task>control, meeting planning criteria.
Task is not a sustained-attention/vigilance paradigm; missing required inclusion criteria VIGILANCE_I1 and VIGILANCE_I2.
Task targets preparation/organization rather than initiation/generation per se; missing required inclusion criteria INITIATION_I1 and INITIATION_I2.

Contrast compares reproduction (requiring preparation) to matching (maintenance) during delayed-response tasks; both are executive-function-related conditions and the contrast isolates task-related executive activation (task vs active control), meeting pooled executive function criteria.

Although both conditions involve working memory, this contrast directly compares two active WM conditions (reproduction vs matching) and does not present a working-memory>control contrast, so WORKING_MEMORY_I2 is not met.
Contrast does not assess inhibitory control; missing required inclusion criteria INHIBITION_I1 and INHIBITION_I2.
Contrast does not assess task-switching or set-shifting; missing required inclusion criteria COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I1 and COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I2.
Reproduction>Matching isolates mental preparation/organization of a forthcoming sequential action (planning) relative to mere maintenance, meeting planning inclusion criteria.
Contrast is not a sustained-attention/vigilance paradigm; missing required inclusion criteria VIGILANCE_I1 and VIGILANCE_I2.
Contrast focuses on preparation/organization of actions rather than initiation/generation per se; missing required inclusion criteria INITIATION_I1 and INITIATION_I2.
